source_text: Prorsus quod in libro meo dixi, cui resistis, verum est: "Nam quod dimissum est in parente, ut trahatur in prole, miris quidem modis fit, sed tamen fit: et quia modus ipse non facili ratione indagatur, nec sermone explicatur, ab infidelibus non creditur" … Quibus verbis meis insidiaris mendaciter, quasi dixerim, "nec ratione comprehendi, nec sermone explicari"; subtrahens inde quod dixi, "non facili" sive "ratione", sive "sermone". Aliud est "nulla", quod tu dicis; aliud est "non facili", quod ego dixi
pass_a_gloss: Altogether what I said in my book, which you resist, is true: 'For that what has been remitted in the parent should be drawn in the offspring happens indeed in marvellous modes, but nevertheless happens: and because the mode itself is not tracked down by easy reason, nor unfolded by speech, by the unbelieving it is not believed'. These words of mine you ambush lyingly, as if I said 'neither to be comprehended by reason, nor to be explained by speech'; withdrawing from there what I said, 'not easy', whether 'reason' or 'speech'. Another thing is 'no', which you say; another is 'not easy', which I said.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “What I said in my book, which you oppose, is entirely true: ‘For that what was forgiven in the parent is passed on in the offspring happens in wonderful ways, but still it happens; and because the way itself is not traced out by easy reasoning, nor explained in speech, unbelievers do not believe it.’ You lay a false trap for these words of mine, as though I had said that it can ‘neither be grasped by reason nor explained in speech,’ taking away from it what I said, ‘not easy,’ whether of ‘reasoning’ or of ‘speech.’ ‘No’ reasoning, which is what you say, is one thing; ‘not easy’ reasoning, which is what I said, is another.”

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
